transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, thank you for seeing me. It's... well, what brings me in is that my head just feels so incredibly cloudy lately, and it's really starting to become a problem at my job. I manage a few community associations, you know, HOAs and condo buildings. I've been doing it a long time. Worked my way up from nothing, honestly, since I left school way back in junior high, so I've always prided myself on being sharp, being the one who can just make a call and get things moving. 

But now... I don't know, I just sit there at my desk. Like last week, I had this board packet to put together for the monthly meeting—just standard stuff, landscaping bids, routine things—and I just stared at it. I stared at this one vendor email about the sprinkler maintenance for I don't know how long. I just couldn't decide what to tell them. It's like my brain is just stuck in thick fog. Simple things, things I used to handle so fast without a second thought, now I can't even make a basic choice about a minor work order. It's just so frustrating because the board members expect answers, and the phones are ringing, and I'm just sitting there staring at the computer screen unable to figure out the simplest next step...
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well, yes, actually. I mean, it's funny you ask that because I was just talking to my sister about this on the phone the other day. She called to ask if I was making my famous Sunday roast—you know, the one with the little pearl onions and the carrots that I usually slow-cook all afternoon. I've been doing that for my family, oh, gosh, for years and years. It's a whole tradition. The grandkids come over, the house smells wonderful, and it's just... it's what I do. It makes me feel like me, if that makes sense. But lately? The thought of even getting the roasting pan out of the cabinet just feels like climbing a mountain. I told her I just couldn't do it. I ended up ordering a pizza for them, which just isn't the same, and I felt terrible about it, but I just had zero desire to stand in the kitchen. 

And it's not just the cooking, either. I've been taking this ballroom dance class on Tuesday nights at the community center. I usually love it—the music, moving around, seeing the other ladies. I even bought these special shoes for it a few months ago. But the last three weeks, I've just sat on my couch and watched the clock tick past the time I should be leaving. I just don't want to go. I don't care about going. Even on the weekends, I usually like to stroll downtown and look at the little art galleries, just window shopping, seeing the new paintings they put up in the windows. I haven't done that in almost a month. It's like all the color has just drained out of everything I usually enjoy. I just... I don't know, I just sit there instead, feeling heavy. It's very unlike me. I usually have so much go in me, you know? But right now, nothing sounds appealing at all.
Has your mood been consistently low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just feeling down some of the time?

Well, you know, it's not like I wake up every single morning and immediately think, "Oh, what a miserable day." It's not quite like that. I mean, some mornings I do manage to get up and make my coffee—I always have this one specific brand, a French roast, that I've been buying from the same little grocery store down the street for probably fifteen years. And while the coffee is brewing, I might feel okay for a minute or two. I might look out the window at the bird feeder and think, "Well, the sun is shining." 

But then... I don't know, it's like this weight just settles over me. And it really does seem to stick around. I wouldn't say it's every single minute of every single day, because like I said, there are those little moments, maybe when my granddaughter sends me a funny picture on my phone, where I smile. But overall? Yeah, I guess it is most of the day. It just feels like I'm dragging myself through mud from the time I get to the office until the time I finally go to bed. And it's been like this for weeks now. I keep hoping I'll just snap out of it, you know? Like maybe a good night's sleep will reset everything, but then the next day comes and it's just that same heavy, flat feeling all over again. So, yes, I suppose it is most of the time, even if there are a few tiny breaks here and there. It's just exhausting, honestly.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you have less energy than usual, even after getting enough rest?

Well, you know, it's funny you mention rest, because I've actually been trying to make sure I get into bed by 9:30 every night. I even bought those blackout curtains—the heavy velvet ones, navy blue, from that department store two towns over, because I thought maybe the streetlamp was keeping me from getting a deep sleep. And I do sleep, I really do. I'll sleep a solid eight, sometimes nine hours. But then I wake up, and... I don't know, it's like I haven't slept at all. 

I'm just so drained. I used to be the kind of person who would jump out of bed, get the coffee going, maybe even sweep the front porch before I left for the office. Now? Just lifting my arms to brush my hair feels like I've been doing heavy lifting all day. I remember last Thursday, I had a full night's sleep, woke up, and just the thought of walking down the hall to the kitchen made me want to lay right back down and close my eyes. I did manage to get up, but my arms and legs just felt like lead. It takes me twice as long to get dressed. I'll put on a blouse, and then I have to sit on the edge of the bed for five minutes just to catch my breath before I can button it. It's not a physical sickness, like a flu or anything, it's just this profound, deep-in-my-bones kind of exhaustion that no amount of sleep seems to touch. I just have no energy to give to anything, and it's making everything take so much longer than it should.
Can you tell me when these feelings first started? Have they been going on for more than two weeks, or have they come and gone before recently?

Well, let me think back... it's a bit complicated, honestly. Because, you see, these stretches—these periods where I just feel so low and heavy—they've actually been coming and going for about a year now. I remember the first time I really noticed it, it was right around the time the daffodils were blooming last spring. I had planted these beautiful King Alfreds all along the front walkway, and I usually take such pride in them, but I just couldn't bring myself to even look at them. So, it's been happening on and off since then. I'll have a few weeks where I'm just dragging, and then it lifts, and I think, "Oh, thank goodness, I'm back to myself." 

But this current stretch... this one feels different. It's definitely been going on for more than two weeks. I'd say it's been a solid month, maybe a little longer, of just this relentless exhaustion and lack of interest. And I really think this latest one is tied to everything that happened after my husband stopped working. He was a machinist for forty years, you know, and when he finally retired, we had all these plans. We were going to fix up the guest room, maybe take a trip up the coast to see the lighthouses. But instead, he's just been underfoot all day, every day, and the dynamic in the house completely shifted. I'm still trying to manage the properties I oversee—which is a whole other headache right now with the new zoning laws they just passed in the next county over—and coming home to him just sitting in his armchair, expecting me to have a plan for the evening... it just became so overwhelming. So, yes, it's been more than two weeks for this current bout, but the whole pattern of these down periods has been going on for about a year, really starting in earnest when he retired and everything at home changed so drastically.
Before this most recent period of feeling down and losing interest in things, have you ever had a time when you felt this way for at least two weeks and it was clearly different from your usual self?

Well, yes, like I was just saying... these stretches where I feel so incredibly low, they've been coming and going for about a year now. It's not just this one time. I remember back in the fall, too, right around the time the leaves started turning—we have this gorgeous maple tree in the front yard that turns the most brilliant shade of red, and usually I love sitting on the porch with a cup of tea just watching the leaves fall. But there was a period back then, definitely lasted a good three weeks, maybe almost a month, where I didn't even want to go out on the porch. I'd just sit in the living room with the blinds drawn. 

So, yes, I've absolutely had times before this current one where I felt just as heavy and empty for weeks at a time, and it was so far from my usual self. I'm normally a doer, you know? I manage properties, I keep things organized, I handle the maintenance schedules and the tenant complaints—which, let me tell you, is a full-time job in itself. But during those down stretches over this past year, I just couldn't manage. I'd let the paperwork pile up on the dining room table, which I hate doing. But like I mentioned, this latest one, the one I'm in right now, it really feels so tied to my husband stopping his work. Because before, the low periods would come, they'd last a few weeks, and eventually, I'd sort of crawl my way out of them. But now, with him home all the time and the whole routine of the house turned upside down, it just feels like I can't catch my breath to even try and pull myself out of it. But yes, to answer your question, this isn't the first time it's lasted for weeks. It's been an on-and-off battle for the whole past year.
Before these past few months, have you had two or more separate periods in your life where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy for at least two weeks at a time?

Well, yes, like I've been saying, it's not just this one time. These stretches... these periods where I just can't seem to find any joy or energy, they've been coming back, on and off, for about a year now. It's like a tide that rolls in and just pulls all the life out of me, and then eventually rolls back out. I've had at least a couple of those stretches before this current one, each lasting a good few weeks, like I mentioned with the daffodils in the spring and the maple leaves in the fall. 

But, you know, even though I've had those episodes over the past year, this latest one... it just feels different. It feels so much heavier, and I really do think it's more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. Because before, I could kind of see a light at the end of the tunnel, even when I was feeling so low. I'd go to work, manage the properties, deal with the tenants—which, like I said, is exhausting in itself, especially with the new zoning laws—and then I'd come home to a quiet house where I could just decompress. But now, with him retired and just... always there, always needing something or expecting me to entertain him, it's like I have no sanctuary anymore. The whole dynamic of our lives changed, and I just don't have the energy to navigate it. So, yes, there were definitely separate periods over this past year where I felt this way for weeks at a time, but this current stretch feels so deeply connected to him being home all the time now. It's just... it's a lot to carry when you already feel like you're walking through mud.

Before this past year, have you ever had multiple separate times in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by periods of at least a couple of months where you felt like your usual self?

Before this past year? Well, no... not that I can recall, not anything like this anyway. I mean, sure, everybody has a bad week here or there, especially in my line of work. You get a tenant who leaves a place a complete disaster—which happened to me a few years back, left the carpets completely ruined and the walls scratched up, and I had to spend weeks fighting with contractors just to get it rentable again—but that was just normal stress, you know? Not this... this heavy, awful, empty feeling. 

So no, these depressed stretches, they've really just been coming back on and off for about a year now. That's when it all really started. And honestly, like I keep trying to explain, even with it happening on and off over the last twelve months, this latest one just feels so much more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. It’s like the straw that broke the camel's back. 

I spent my whole life working hard, you know? I didn't even make it past the eighth grade, but I built up my business managing these properties through sheer grit and common sense. I was always the one who kept all the plates spinning. But then he retires from the machine shop, and suddenly my whole routine is just gone. He used to be out of the house by six in the morning, regular as a clock! Now I'm trying to balance the association ledgers at the kitchen table, and he's wandering in asking what's for lunch at ten-thirty in the morning. It just drains whatever little energy I had managed to build back up after those other low stretches earlier in the year. So, before a year ago? No, I was always on the go, always fine. It’s just been this past year of it coming and going, and then this current stretch just weighing me down completely now that he's home all the time.
Have you ever had periods where your mood was unusually high, you felt extremely energetic, or you were more irritable than usual for several days at a time?

Well, yes... I suppose I have. But it's not like this awful, heavy feeling I have now. It's almost the exact opposite, actually. There have been times, you know, just for a few days here and there, where I felt... I don't know, almost too bright? Like I was running on a different kind of fuel. I remember a few months back, right before one of those awful low stretches hit me, I had this burst where I just felt so bold and full of ideas. 

We had our monthly community association meeting—we hold it in the basement of the old Methodist church, which always smells a little like damp cardboard, but it’s cheap—and I was just... I was on fire, I guess you could say. I had all these plans for how we needed to restructure the maintenance contracts, and I just couldn't wait to get them out. I remember talking right over poor Mr. Henderson, who’s been the treasurer since the nineties and talks about as fast as molasses in January. I just couldn't slow down to let him finish his sentences. I felt like I had to get everything said right that second. 

And I felt so energetic, like I could take on the world, but it also made me... prickly, I guess. Because I'd come home from those meetings, still buzzing, and my husband would do something so minor, like leave his boots by the back door instead of putting them on the mat, and I would just snap at him. I mean, really bite his head off over nothing at all. It was like all that bright energy just turned into this sharp, irritable edge the minute I walked through the door and saw him sitting there. So, yes, I’ve definitely had those few days where I felt unusually high and energetic, but also incredibly short-tempered, especially with him. It's like a switch flips, and suddenly I'm a completely different person than the one who can't even get off the couch.
How long did those unusually high or energetic moods usually last—were they just for a day or two, or did they go on for several days in a row?

Well, it's not just a day or two in a vacuum, if you know what I mean. It’s hard to just put a neat little bow on it and say it lasted exactly this many hours or days, because it all just bleeds together with everything happening at the house right now. But if I really sit and think about the timing of it all... this sharper change in my energy, you know, that big burst of confidence where I felt like I could take on the world and reorganize the whole association, and then crashing right down into that low, cloudy feeling... it's all been going on for about two weeks. 

And I know exactly why it's been two weeks, because that is exactly when my husband retired and was suddenly home all day. Two weeks ago this past Friday. They gave him a little watch at the machine shop, they had a grocery store sheet cake, and then Monday morning rolls around and he just... doesn't leave. He's just sitting there at the kitchen table with his coffee while I'm trying to sort through the plumbing receipts for the duplex on Elm Street. 

So for these past two weeks, with him just suddenly in my space all day long, I’ve been having these sharp, intense shifts. The energy and confidence will just shoot through the roof, and I'm buzzing around, snapping at him to get out of my way or move his newspaper so I can work, and then it all just gives out and I sink right back into that heavy, low, cloudy feeling where I can't even bring myself to look at my ledger. It's just been this constant, exhausting back-and-forth for two solid weeks now. I used to have the whole day to pace myself, to do my work in peace, but now that he's retired and just... always there, always underfoot, it's like my whole system is just completely out of whack.

You mentioned feeling unusually energetic and irritable for a few days at a time. Did any of those periods last for four days or longer, where your mood was clearly different from your usual self and stayed elevated for most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Four days? Well, now... four whole days in a row, from morning till night? No, I wouldn't say it's ever been quite that long. 

You see, it’s just hard to hold onto that kind of bright, buzzing energy for four entire days when you’ve got as much on your plate as I do, especially with how things are now. Like I was saying, my husband is just always... he's just always *there* now. So maybe I wake up on a Tuesday feeling like a firecracker, you know? Just completely on top of the world, ready to march down to the bank and sort out the escrow accounts for the townhomes on Maple Street. Because let me tell you, the bank always, always messes up the escrow if you don't watch them like a hawk. I've been keeping these books since long before computers did all the math for you, so I know when something's off by even a penny. 

But anyway, I'll have all that energy, and I'll be flying through my work, maybe getting a bit snappy with him because he's standing in the middle of the kitchen asking where the good coffee filters went while I'm trying to balance a ledger. But does it last four whole days? No, no, I really don't think it stretches out that long without breaking. Because by day two, or maybe day three at the absolute most, the energy just sort of... it just fizzles out. Or I get so exhausted from being frustrated with him being underfoot, or arguing with a plumber, that I just crash right back down into that heavy, awful feeling. 

I remember just last week, I started off Monday feeling grand, just full of ideas, got the gutters cleaned out at the triplex, argued down the landscaper's new estimate... but by Wednesday afternoon, I was completely done. I was just sitting in the recliner, staring at the wall, and I couldn't even bring myself to open the afternoon mail. So, four days straight of feeling high and mighty and irritable all day long? No, it never stays stuck like that for that long. It just flares up for a couple of days, maybe three if I really push it, and then it's gone again. You just can't sustain it, not with the house feeling this crowded all of a sudden.
Can you tell me if there was ever a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, even before the past year?

Before the past year? Well, let me think on that. No, I wouldn't really say it goes back further than that. If I'm being honest—and I keep a pretty close eye on the calendar because you have to when you're tracking lease renewals and quarterly taxes—these depressed stretches... they've been coming back on and off for just about a year now. Not before that, no. 

For the last year, it's just been this cycle where I'll get so down and lose interest in everything for a few weeks at a time. I'd sit there and I wouldn't even care if the gutters were backing up at the Elm Street duplex, which just isn't like me at all. I've always prided myself on staying on top of the maintenance. But then the cloud would eventually lift, and I'd get back to normal for a while. So it's been coming and going like that for about twelve months. 

But this latest one, this awful heavy feeling I have right now? This one feels different, and it feels much more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. Like I was telling you, him retiring just threw my whole world completely out of balance. Before, when I had one of these low stretches over the past year, I could at least just sit in the quiet of my own home and try to wait it out. I didn't have to put on a brave face or explain why I wasn't getting up to cook. But now that he's stopped working and he's just... always sitting right there in the living room, wanting a sandwich at noon sharp or asking me where the newspaper went... I just can't handle it. I can't even find the energy to answer him half the time, and it just drags me right down deeper. So, yes, it's been about a year of these stretches coming and going, but this current one is absolutely because of the change with him being home all the time now.

Before this past year, have you ever had two or more separate times in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by at least two months where you felt like your usual self?

Before this past year? Two or more times... no. No, I really can't say that I did. Because, well, you have to understand how my life was before all this started. When you’re managing properties—and I’ve been doing this a long, long time, ever since we bought our first little rental over on 4th Street back in the eighties—you just don't have the luxury of losing interest in things for two whole weeks. 

I mean, if a tenant calls because the heat is out in the middle of January, or the roof is leaking into their kitchen, you can't just say, 'Oh, I'm feeling a bit down, let me just sit here and I'll call the furnace guy next month.' It doesn't work like that in real estate. You have to get up, put your boots on, and go deal with it right then and there. 

So no, I never had these big stretches of feeling low like that in the past, not separated by two months or however you put it. I was always just going, going, going. Keeping the books, collecting the rent checks, making sure the landscaping got done before the city complained about the grass getting too high. I didn't have the time or the space to just sit in the recliner and stare at the wall back then. It really is just this past twelve months that this heavy, awful feeling started creeping in on me. Before that? I was just my usual self, day in and day out, year after year. I was always the one keeping everything running smoothly, until... well, until this past year, and especially now with him being home all the time and messing up my routine.

Before this past year, have you ever had two or more separate times when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by at least two months where you felt like your usual self?

Well, like I was just saying a minute ago... maybe I didn't explain it right, or maybe you're asking something just a little bit different that I'm not quite catching? But no, before this past year, I really didn't have anything like that. Two or more times? No. 

I mean, I just didn't have the luxury for it, doctor. When you leave school in the eighth grade to start working like I did, you figure out real fast that nobody is going to pay your bills if you're just sitting around feeling sorry for yourself. You just have to keep moving. And then once we bought that first rental property, it was constant. I'd be up at the crack of dawn, driving over to check if the painters actually used the primer we paid for—because let me tell you, contractors will skip the primer every single time if you aren't standing right over their shoulder watching them—and then I'd be up late at the kitchen table with my calculator and the ledger. 

There just wasn't a two-week window anywhere in my life to lose interest in things! If I lost interest, the pipes would freeze, or a tenant would skip out on rent, or the city would fine us for the trash not being hauled away properly. I had to care about every little detail. So, no, before these last twelve months, I was always just my regular, busy self. It's only been this past year that this heavy cloud started coming around, and like I said, it's just become unbearable now with my husband sitting in his recliner all day long asking me what's for lunch. But before a year ago? No, never.

Before this past year, have you ever had two or more separate times when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by at least two months where you felt like your usual self?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. Are you sure you're looking at the right notes? Because I swear you just asked me that exact same thing, word for word. And the answer is still no. I never had anything like that happen before this past year. Not two times, not one time, not with two months in between... just no. 

I don't know how many different ways I can explain it, but my life just didn't allow for it. I remember back in, oh, it must have been '98, we had that massive ice storm that knocked out the power all down Elm Street. I was out there at five in the morning with fifty-pound bags of rock salt, making sure the walkways at the duplexes were clear so nobody would slip and sue us. You think I could have just stayed in bed for two weeks feeling down? Absolutely not. I was always the one keeping the wheels turning. 

It really, truly is just this past year that things changed. That's when this heavy feeling started coming and going. And like I keep telling you, it's because my routine got entirely turned upside down with my husband retiring. He used to be out of the house all day, and I had my system. Now he's just planted in the living room, staring at me, expecting me to wait on him hand and foot while I'm trying to balance the checkbooks. So, no, doctor. Nothing before a year ago. Just this past year.

Before this past year, have you ever had two or more separate times when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by at least two months where you felt like your usual self?

Doctor, are you... are you feeling quite alright today? Because I am starting to wonder if maybe we need to check *your* hearing, or if you're just reading from a script and not actually listening to a word I'm saying. That is the exact same question you just asked me. Again. For the fourth time, I think? 

But fine, fine, I will say it again, and maybe this time it will stick. No. Before this past year, I did not have these two-week stretches of feeling down. It has *only* been this past year. These depressed stretches, these heavy, awful periods where I just can't seem to care about the properties or anything else... they have been coming back on and off for about a year now. That's it. Just a year. 

And like I've been trying to tell you, this latest stretch, the one I'm in right now, it feels so much more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. He retired, he came home, and he just... stayed there. In my space. All day long. I used to have my mornings to myself to go over the tenant ledgers, call the plumbers, organize the receipts for the accountant... I had a system! A beautiful, efficient system that kept everything running like a top. And now? Now I can't even sit at the kitchen table with my calculator without him asking me where the remote is, or what we're doing for dinner, or if I can make him a sandwich. It's suffocating. It really is. It just drains the life right out of me. So yes, the on-and-off stretches started about a year ago, but this current one is definitely because of him being home all the time. Before a year ago? Never. I was too busy working to be depressed.

Before this past year, have you ever had two or more separate times when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and those times were separated by at least two months where you felt like your usual self?

Doctor... honestly, are we being filmed? Is this some sort of hidden camera show? Or did the record skip? Because I swear on my life, you have asked me that exact same question over and over and over today. Are you even listening to me? I don't mean to be rude, but I am practically blue in the face telling you the same thing! 

No. Before this past year, no. Never. I didn't have time for it. 

I'll say it again, just in case you didn't write it down the first four times. These depressed stretches, these awful periods where I just can't get out of bed and I don't care about the rental properties or the tenants or anything... they have only been coming back on and off for about a year. Just one year. Twelve months. That is it. 

And like I keep trying to explain to you, this latest one, the one I am stuck in right this very minute, it feels so much more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. He retired, he came home, and he ruined my entire routine. I used to have my mornings! I'd get up, make my coffee, sit at the island in the kitchen with my ledger and my calculator, and I would get things done. I managed five duplexes and a four-unit building all by myself. You don't do that by sitting around feeling sorry for yourself. But now? Now he's just... there. All the time. Asking me what's on TV, asking me if we have any more of those little powdered donuts, asking me to find his reading glasses. It's like having a toddler in the house, but it's a grown man who used to work forty hours a week! It just drained everything right out of me. So yes, the on-and-off stretches started about a year ago, but this one right now? It's because of him. Before a year ago, I was fine. I was busy. I was working. Do you understand what I'm saying now, doctor, or are you going to ask me again?
